clue.text: A little lift for Manuel, maybe

definitions.meaning: a small hoist carrying food between floors of a restaurant or house
Manuel is the hapless Spanish server in the British sitcom Fawlty Towers, who barely speaks English

explanation.surface: A small hoist installed for the benefit of a hotel's put-upon Spanish employee.
explanation.walkthrough: Manuel, from the 1970s BBC sitcom Fawlty Towers, is a waiter who can say almost nothing in English, hence 'dumb'.
explanation.definitionFit: A food hoist between kitchen and dining room bears this name, and a near-speechless server fits the phrase taken literally.

clue.text: Testify to remove ruler

definitions.meaning: to give sworn evidence, especially in a written statement
to oust a king or leader from power

explanation.surface: Someone takes the witness stand in order to bring down a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both sworn testimony in law and ousting a monarch from the throne.

clue.text: Providing me with dodgy gear is inadequate

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or shady, so these letters are tampered with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Supplying someone with faulty equipment isn't good enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something scanty or insufficient falls short of what is needed.

clue.text: The drinkers are just animals at this pub!

definitions.text: The drinkers are just animals at this pub!

parts.words: The drinkers are just animals at this pub!
parts.note: read as a jibe about rowdy pub drinkers, but taken literally it describes a pool where wild animals gather to drink, also a slang name for a bar

explanation.surface: A complaint that the regulars at some pub behave like beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a waterhole frequented by wildlife and, informally, a pub.

clue.text: Measure used in central heating

parts.note: taken as written
CH is the standard abbreviation for central heating, as in British property ads

explanation.surface: A unit of measurement applied to a heating system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is just a link; CH for central heating is common in British house-sale listings.
explanation.definitionFit: An imperial unit of length, one twelfth of a foot.

clue.text: Reseal most faulty rubbery materials

indicators.note: faulty means defective, so the letters of the words before it are put right by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Instructions to seal again the majority of defective rubber goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic polymers such as natural or synthetic rubber, which stretch and spring back.

clue.text: Discontinue returning jars

indicators.note: returning means the word for jars is read backwards

parts.note: jars are pots

explanation.surface: Someone stops a product line because the containers keep coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to cease or halt something.

clue.text: Almost frighten 4, oddly, which is great!

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to frighten is to terrify

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third and so on letters of the answer at 4

explanation.surface: Nearly scaring someone, strangely, turns out to be wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the last letter of TERRIFY to leave TERRIF; 'oddly' takes the odd letters I and C of INCH, the answer to 4 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: informally, excellent or marvellous.

clue.text: Expecting first price ruling

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

explanation.surface: Anticipating the initial price decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expecting' looks like part of the surface's anticipation but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is an everyday euphemism for carrying a baby.

clue.text: Credit card needs secure carrier

parts.note: plastic is slang for a credit card
to bag something is to secure or obtain it

explanation.surface: Advice that a credit card requires a safe holder.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers call a plastic shopping bag a carrier, short for carrier bag.

clue.text: Right to take payment? Just the opposite, it's gratis

indicators.note: to take would have the letter for right swallow the payment, putting one inside the other
just the opposite reverses the stated arrangement, so the payment swallows the right letter instead

parts.note: a fee is a payment

explanation.surface: Someone argues about the entitlement to charge, only to be told it costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right to take payment' would be R round FEE; 'Just the opposite' flips it, so FEE takes R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: given without charge.

clue.text: George's figure, for example — is he too good to be true?

definitions.meaning: a cast statuette of St George, the kind of devotional image made of plaster

definitions.text: is he too good to be true?
definitions.meaning: someone who appears morally faultless, often hypocritically so

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a statue of George depicts someone suspiciously virtuous.
explanation.walkthrough: St George is England's patron saint; plaster statuettes of saints were common church figures.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a moulded saint's statue and a person who pretends to perfect virtue.

clue.text: Rarest kind of philosopher — an existentialist

indicators.note: kind of suggests a variety or version of the word before, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rare sort of thinker, one belonging to the existentialist school.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul, the French thinker, was a leading figure of existentialism.

clue.text: The way Alabama wild cat takes a horse

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama
a lion is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A big cat on an Alabama road catches a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, kept for breeding.

clue.text: Melvyn on art — luvvy first and last, in a boastful way!

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the presenter's name comes before the next word

parts.note: Melvyn Bragg is a British broadcaster and writer known for arts programmes
taken as written

indicators.note: first and last means take only the opening and closing letters of the word

explanation.surface: A TV arts presenter holds forth on art, theatrical gush first and foremost.
explanation.walkthrough: Melvyn Bragg presented the long-running British arts show The South Bank Show; 'luvvy' is British slang for a gushing actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb formed from the word for a show-off, meaning boastfully.

clue.text: Insertion made in preface for religious outfit

parts.note: an intro is a preface or introduction
a mission is a religious organisation sent out to spread a faith

explanation.surface: Something added in the foreword about a church organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made in' and 'for' are link words joining definition and pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal term for introducing or putting one thing into another.

clue.text: Peculiar people on back-street, looking for bits and pieces

parts.note: peculiar means odd
men are people

indicators.note: back means the abbreviation for street is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Strange folk in a back alley hunting for scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-street' reads as one word for a seedy alley, but 'back' is the reversal signal working on 'street'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: leftover scraps or odds and ends.

clue.text: Urge girl to take note of timer

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
G is a musical note
a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Encouraging a young woman to pay attention to a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take' and 'of' are link words; LASS takes G in front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sand-filled hourglass used to time boiling.

clue.text: To understand the plot, do some spadework

definitions.meaning: dig is slang for understand, and the garden is a plot of land, so read as grasping the plot
literally turning over soil in a yard

explanation.surface: Grasping the storyline takes some hard preparatory work.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: DIG (understand, 1960s slang) + THE GARDEN (the plot).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means literally turning soil with a spade, and cryptically grasping the plot.

clue.text: Are leaving out margarine, it's more than is necessary

indicators.note: leaving out means the letters of the first word are dropped from the spread named after it

explanation.surface: Skipping the spread is overdoing it, someone insists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving out' removes the A, R and E of 'Are' from MARGARINE, in order, to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A margin is an amount in excess, as in a margin for error or safety.

clue.text: Marie gets 6 and two quarters

parts.note: the answer to 6 across
E and S, east and south, are two of the compass quarters

explanation.surface: A woman named Marie receives six items and a couple of quarter-shares.
explanation.walkthrough: Marie Stopes was a British pioneer of birth control; 6 refers to the answer at 6 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Marie is the first name of the British family-planning campaigner.

clue.text: Publication the Spanish left to an explorer

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication
el is Spanish for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish magazine bequeathed to a famous voyager.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferdinand, the Portuguese navigator, led the first expedition to sail around the world.

clue.text: Inclined to give Lewis's lion a bone

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C S Lewis's Narnia books
T, from the T-bone, a steak whose bone is shaped like that letter

explanation.surface: Feeling disposed to toss a bone to a storybook lion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give' and 'a' are link words; the setter takes 'bone' as the letter T, as in T-bone steak.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: slanting or at an angle.

clue.text: Troupes for troops

parts.note: performing companies laid on to entertain soldiers, the wartime British forces entertainment body

explanation.surface: Theatre companies sent to amuse servicemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Entertainments National Service Association put on shows for British forces in the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Initials of the wartime organisation that staged concert parties for the armed forces.

clue.text: Almost getting close

explanation.surface: Nearly drawing close to something.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means both nearly and nearby, as in 'near perfect' and 'near the shops'.

clue.text: Erect pugin's tan edifice with date added

indicators.note: an edifice is something built, so the letters are constructed into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written with the S

explanation.surface: Admiring a tan-coloured building by the Victorian architect Pugin, with its date added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edifice' acts as the anagram signal, building PUGINS and TAN plus D into the answer; Pugin was a Victorian Gothic-revival architect.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: upright, on one's feet.

clue.text: Elite soldiers go head first into window

parts.note: the SAS, Special Air Service, is the British army's elite unit

indicators.note: first means take only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Special forces dive headlong through a window.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a sliding window frame, as in a sash window.

clue.text: Old people breaking out in zits, Ben? Nay!

indicators.note: breaking out suggests something erupting into disorder, so the letters are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Someone asks Ben whether he has spots, and is told no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out in zits' looks like acne; 'breaking out' shuffles ZITS, BEN and NAY together, with 'in' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhabitants of Byzantium, the ancient city later Constantinople.
